# @entirehq mention watcher

Someone replies to `@entirehq` on X, or posts a link to entire.io without
tagging anyone. You find out four hours later, because nobody had that search
tab open.

This closes that gap. A daemon polls one live search for both the handle and
the domain every five minutes, triages every new mention, and posts it to
Slack in one of two shapes so the ones worth acting on do not read like the
rest.

```
★ `REPLY` @HaimantikaM · 17k followers
> Great points! We are also building something for this, would
> love to give you early access.
View on X · not a follower, offers early access · Oct 14 at 11:57 AM

`REPLY` @devsdv_ · @haatifff @neatlogs @EntireHQ Thanks 👍 · open · 172 followers

`CHAIN` 9 more replies in this thread · @Archilyte_, @j3rah_, @catmanyau, +4 · open
```

Priority gets a card and a `★` in the notification text; routine collapses to
one line, and a thread that keeps going collapses to a count. Every line leads with its kind in the same slot (`TWEET`, `REPLY`,
`QUOTE`), so the left edge answers "reply or tweet?" without reading the line.
A post that linked the site without tagging the account reads `linked
entire.io` instead of `replied to @entirehq`, because it did not.
On a live sample of 20 mentions this put 1 in priority and 16 in routine, with
3 muted.

It runs as a launchd agent — at login, across reboots, restarted if it dies,
independent of whether Claude Code is open. Zero tokens: a plain Node process
posting to a webhook, not an agent.

## Setup

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env       # fill in the five values below
npm run check              # one live scrape, printed, notifies nobody
npm run install-agent      # install + start the daemon
```

| Variable | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` | browserbase.com → Settings |
| `BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID` | same page |
| `X_AUTH_TOKEN` | logged-in x.com tab → DevTools → Application → Cookies → `auth_token` |
| `X_CSRF_TOKEN` | same place → `ct0` |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` | api.slack.com/apps → your app → Incoming Webhooks |

Optional: `X_WATCH_POLL_MS` (`300000`), `X_CHAIN_LIMIT` (`3`),
`X_OWN_HANDLE` (`entirehq`),
`X_BRAND_DOMAIN` (`entire.io`), `X_SEARCH_QUERY` (defaults to
`(@entirehq OR "entire.io")`, built from the two above),
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `X_MUTE_HANDLES`, `X_TEAM_HANDLES`.

Config is read once at boot — after editing `.env`, re-run `install-agent`.

**Why cookies, not the X API.** Live search is login-gated, and API v2's
recent-search endpoint needs a paid tier (~$200/mo). Two cookies cost nothing
and last months; when they expire the watcher says so in Slack rather than
returning nothing, which would read as "nobody is mentioning us."

## How it works

```
launchd (RunAtLoad, KeepAlive) → watch.mjs
   ↓
   scrape ──→ parse ──→ filter ──→ diff ──→ post to Slack
   Browserbase   X's own    drop our     seen-id     Block Kit
   + Playwright  JSON       own posts,   store       webhook
                 (DOM        label kind
                  fallback)  and match
   ↓
   sleep 5m, repeat
```

- **Claude Code's hooks are a fallback.** `SessionStart`/`SessionEnd` run a
  session-scoped watcher only when no agent is installed for this project. With
  the agent installed they stand down, so notifications never double up.
- **Slack is the only channel.** Nothing prints to your terminal; diagnostics
  go to `.claude/entirehq-watcher/watch.log` — including when Slack is the
  thing that's broken.
- **The handle and the domain are one query, not two polls.** The search is
  `(@entirehq OR "entire.io")`, so a link share with no tag is caught at the
  same cost as before: one Browserbase session per poll. Each mention records
  how it matched (handle, link, or both), and Slack and the classifier both
  read that, since a link share is not addressed to anyone and the author is
  not waiting on a reply.
- **A link is invisible in the tweet text.** X rewrites every URL in
  `full_text` to `t.co`, so the domain can only be matched against the
  expanded URLs in `entities.urls` (the link's display text, on the DOM
  fallback path). Matching the text alone would have found nothing.
- **A thread gets a budget, not a line per reply.** One account thanking
  twelve people one reply at a time is twelve mentions and one thread. The
  first `X_CHAIN_LIMIT` routine mentions from a thread post normally; the rest
  collapse into a single `CHAIN` line naming who is in it. The budget is
  charged in the store and lasts six hours, so a thread that drips in two
  replies per poll cannot restart it every five minutes. Priority is never
  collapsed and never charged: a quiet channel is worth less than one
  actionable mention.
- **Collapsing happens after triage, not before.** The tier has to be known
  first or a real support question could disappear into a count. It costs
  nothing extra: every new mention was already being classified one at a time.
- **Two signals decide the tier, and they answer different questions.** A
  deterministic score measures reach (follower count, whether the author
  already follows `@entirehq`, verified, question, quote vs deep reply,
  switching intent). Claude Haiku reads the text and judges intent. A verdict
  wins whenever the classifier ran: reach does not make an emoji reply worth
  answering. The score decides alone when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset or the
  call fails, so an outage degrades the ranking instead of dropping the post.
- **Engagement counts are deliberately unused.** A mention is seen within one
  poll of being posted, when every tweet still reads 0 likes and ~20 views, so
  traction cannot rank anything at the moment the decision has to be made.
  Author reach is known immediately; traction is not.
- **`IGNORE` demotes, it never drops.** A classifier false negative on a real
  support question would be invisible, and silence is the failure this tool
  exists to prevent. Only `X_MUTE_HANDLES` suppresses outright.
- **It reads X's JSON, not the page.** Playwright intercepts the
  `SearchTimeline` response instead of scraping `data-testid` attributes X
  rotates at will. Reply/quote classification uses real fields
  (`in_reply_to_status_id`, `is_quote_status`). DOM extraction is a labelled
  fallback.
- **Seen only once Slack accepts it.** Marking a failed post as seen would drop
  that mention permanently and silently; a failure costs one duplicate attempt
  next poll instead.
- **The first run notifies nobody.** It baselines whatever is already on the
  page, or day one dumps every existing mention into Slack.
- **It won't shut up about being broken.** Expired cookies, scrapes stuck at
  the 30-minute backoff cap, and three consecutive empty polls each fire
  exactly one Slack alert, deduped through the store so restarts don't
  re-alarm.

## Known limitations

- **One page per poll** — no scrolling, so roughly X's first ~20 results.
  Heavier bursts overflow; the watcher logs a note when a poll comes back that
  full. Shorter `X_WATCH_POLL_MS` reduces the risk at the cost of more sessions.
  Both terms share that one page, so a burst of replies to the account can
  crowd out a link share posted in the same window. A live check on Oct 17
  came back 20 of 20 full, 19 of them replies in one tag chain.
- **A link match is only as good as X's index.** The domain is searched as a
  quoted phrase, so a post that writes "entire dot io", links a shortener, or
  embeds the URL in an image is not found. Neither is one whose link X has
  not indexed yet.
- **A collapsed reply is never shown again.** The `CHAIN` line is its only
  delivery: it is marked seen once that line lands, so the text of a routine
  reply past the budget lives on X and nowhere else. The thread link is in the
  line for exactly that reason.
- **Threads are only groupable on the JSON path.** `conversation_id_str` does
  not exist in the rendered page, so under the DOM fallback a chain is grouped
  by author instead. One account replying repeatedly still collapses; three
  accounts piling into one thread do not.
- **Muting is by handle, not by person.** `X_OWN_HANDLE` drops the brand
  account, `X_MUTE_HANDLES` drops named accounts entirely, and
  `X_TEAM_HANDLES` pins teammates to the routine tier (their replies are a
  receipt, not a call to action).
- **One agent per machine** — the launchd label is fixed. A second checkout
  sees the plist names a different project and falls back to its hooks.
- **Automated browsing is contrary to X's ToS** — accepted knowingly, for one
  account's own brand mentions at low volume.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run install-agent` | Install and start the daemon (idempotent) |
| `npm run uninstall-agent` | Stop and remove it; hooks take over again |
| `npm run preview` | Triages one live scrape and prints the tiers. Posts nothing |
| `npm run check` | One live scrape, dry-run, notifies nobody |
| `npm test` | 181 tests: config, both parsers, filter, store, notifiers, launchd, triage, chains |
| `tail -f .claude/entirehq-watcher/watch.log` | What the daemon is doing |

One Browserbase session per poll — 288/day at the default, now continuous
rather than only while an editor is open. One Haiku call per *new* mention
(not per poll), so classifier spend tracks mention volume, not uptime: tens of
calls a day at current volume, cents a month.

## Layout

| Path | |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/config.mjs` | Loads and validates `.env`; native `loadEnvFile` |
| `scripts/x-scrape.mjs` | Browserbase session, cookies, JSON interception, DOM fallback |
| `scripts/parse.mjs` | Both payload shapes → normalized records. Pure |
| `scripts/filter.mjs` | Drops our own posts, labels mention/reply/quote and handle/link. Pure |
| `scripts/store.mjs` | Seen-id cache, 500-id cap, baseline and alert flags |
| `scripts/score.mjs` | Deterministic reach/shape score and handle lists. Pure |
| `scripts/classify.mjs` | Claude Haiku intent triage; resolves, never throws |
| `scripts/tier.mjs` | Combines score and verdict into a tier. Pure |
| `scripts/chain.mjs` | Groups a batch by thread and spends the per-thread budget. Pure |
| `scripts/notify-slack.mjs` | Tiered Block Kit payloads, webhook POST, one retry |
| `scripts/preview.mjs` | Dry-run triage of one live scrape |
| `scripts/notify-terminal.mjs` | ANSI output — `check.mjs` only |
| `scripts/watch.mjs` | The poll loop: backoff, alerting, logging, shutdown |
| `scripts/launchd.mjs` | Plist generation, per-project ownership check. Pure |
| `scripts/install-agent.mjs` / `uninstall-agent.mjs` | Daemon lifecycle |
| `scripts/hook-start.mjs` / `hook-stop.mjs` | Session-scoped fallback |

Node ≥ 20.12, ESM, three runtime dependencies (`@browserbasehq/sdk`,
`playwright-core`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), zero test dependencies — the suite is
`node:test`. `parse`, `filter`, `store`, `launchd`, `score`, and `tier` are
pure functions, which is why the logic is testable without a network.

## How this was built

Spec → plan → ten TDD tasks, each implemented by one agent and reviewed by
another. Design doc and plan are in `docs/superpowers/`, committed before any
code was written.

Review caught six defects that originated in the plan itself — a `node --test`
invocation that silently exits 1 on Node 24+, a Browserbase session leaked on
every connect failure (billable), and a store that marked a batch seen *before*
announcing it, losing the remainder if killed mid-batch.

The first live run exposed the one thing no test could: the watcher had never
actually run. It only existed while a Claude Code session was open — which is
what the launchd agent replaced.

The first live run of the triage did the same. With `tool_choice: auto` about
one Haiku call in six answered in prose instead of calling the tool, and
letting a high score override an explicit `ROUTINE` verdict put eleven
emoji-only tag-chain replies from a single account into priority. Forcing the
tool call and letting the verdict win took priority from 13 of 20 to 1 of 20.
{
  "name": "entirehq-mention-watcher",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "description": "Watches the @entirehq live search on X and announces new mentions in the Claude Code terminal and Slack.",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "node --test \"test/**/*.test.mjs\"",
    "check": "node scripts/check.mjs",
    "install-agent": "node scripts/install-agent.mjs",
    "uninstall-agent": "node scripts/uninstall-agent.mjs",
    "preview": "node scripts/preview.mjs"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@anthropic-ai/sdk": "^0.133.0",
    "@browserbasehq/sdk": "^2.15.0",
    "playwright-core": "^1.61.1"
  },
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=20.12"
  }
}
import { MATCH_LINK, MATCH_BOTH } from './filter.mjs';

const VERB = {
  mention: 'mentioned',
  reply: 'replied to',
  quote: 'quoted',
};

// Only used by callers that have no config in hand (the tests). The watcher
// passes the live values, so a renamed account or domain cannot drift.
const BRAND = { handle: 'entirehq', domain: 'entire.io' };

const MAX_BODY = 500;

// Slack mrkdwn treats these three as control characters. Tweet text is
// untrusted input — without this a tweet could forge a link in our channel.
export function escapeSlack(text) {
  return String(text)
    .replace(/&/g, '&')
    .replace(/</g, '<')
    .replace(/>/g, '>');
}

function body(text) {
  const flat = String(text).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  return flat.length > MAX_BODY ? `${flat.slice(0, MAX_BODY - 1)}…` : flat;
}

function reach(tweet) {
  const n = Number(tweet.followers);
  if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n <= 0) return null;
  if (n >= 10000) return `${Math.round(n / 1000)}k followers`;
  if (n >= 1000) return `${(n / 1000).toFixed(1)}k followers`;
  return `${n} followers`;
}

function meta(tweet, triage) {
  const r = reach(tweet);
  const reasons = (triage?.reasons ?? []).filter((x) => x !== r);
  return reasons.slice(0, 3).join(', ') || tweet.kind;
}

// Priority gets the full card and a leading marker; routine collapses to one
// line. The whole point of the split is that a skimming reader can tell them
// apart without reading either, so the shapes must differ, not just the words.
// The kind leads every line, in the same slot on both tiers, so scanning the
// left edge answers "reply or tweet?" without reading the line. It used to sit
// mid-chain in the trailing metadata, where it was effectively invisible.
const KIND_LABEL = {
  mention: 'TWEET',
  reply: 'REPLY',
  quote: 'QUOTE',
};

export function kindLabel(kind) {
  return KIND_LABEL[kind] ?? 'TWEET';
}

// What the post did to us. A link-only share never tagged the account, so the
// reply/quote verb would misreport it: the kind label already carries whether
// it was a reply, and the verb slot has to say what it matched on instead.
function action(tweet, brand) {
  if (tweet.matchedVia === MATCH_LINK) return `linked ${brand.domain}`;
  return `${VERB[tweet.kind] ?? 'mentioned'} @${brand.handle}`;
}

function linkTag(tweet, brand) {
  return tweet.matchedVia === MATCH_LINK || tweet.matchedVia === MATCH_BOTH
    ? `links ${brand.domain}`
    : null;
}

export function buildTweetMessage(tweet, triage = null, brand = BRAND) {
  const did = action(tweet, brand);
  const epoch = Math.floor(new Date(tweet.createdAt).getTime() / 1000);
  const handle = escapeSlack(tweet.author);
  const profile = `https://x.com/${encodeURIComponent(tweet.author)}`;
  const label = kindLabel(tweet.kind);
  const r = reach(tweet);
  const tag = linkTag(tweet, brand);

  if (triage && triage.tier === 'routine') {
    return {
      text: `${label} \u00b7 @${handle} ${did}`,
      blocks: [
        {
          type: 'context',
          elements: [
            {
              type: 'mrkdwn',
              text:
                `\`${label}\` <${profile}|@${handle}> \u00b7 ` +
                `${escapeSlack(body(tweet.text).slice(0, 140))} \u00b7 ` +
                [`<${tweet.url}|open>`, r, tag].filter(Boolean).join(' \u00b7 '),
            },
          ],
        },
      ],
    };
  }

  return {
    text: `\u2605 ${label} \u00b7 @${handle} ${did}`,
    blocks: [
      {
        type: 'section',
        text: {
          type: 'mrkdwn',
          text:
            `*\u2605 \`${label}\`* <${profile}|@${handle}>` +
            (r ? ` \u00b7 ${r}` : '') +
            `\n>${escapeSlack(body(tweet.text))}`,
        },
      },
      {
        type: 'context',
        elements: [
          {
            type: 'mrkdwn',
            text: [
              `<${tweet.url}|View on X>`,
              escapeSlack(meta(tweet, triage)),
              tag,
              `<!date^${epoch}^{date_short_pretty} at {time}|${tweet.createdAt}>`,
            ]
              .filter(Boolean)
              .join(' \u00b7 '),
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  };
}

// The one line a thread gets once it is out of budget. It names who is in it
// and where to open it; the posts themselves are routine by definition, so
// the count is the information.
export function buildChainMessage({ count, authors = [], moreAuthors = 0, url }) {
  const noun = count === 1 ? 'reply' : 'replies';
  const who = [
    ...authors.map((author) => `@${escapeSlack(author)}`),
    moreAuthors > 0 ? `+${moreAuthors}` : null,
  ]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(', ');

  return {
    text: `CHAIN \u00b7 ${count} more ${noun} in this thread`,
    blocks: [
      {
        type: 'context',
        elements: [
          {
            type: 'mrkdwn',
            text: [`\`CHAIN\` ${count} more ${noun} in this thread`, who, `<${url}|open>`]
              .filter(Boolean)
              .join(' \u00b7 '),
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  };
}

export function buildAlertMessage(text) {
  return {
    text,
    blocks: [{ type: 'section', text: { type: 'mrkdwn', text: escapeSlack(text) } }],
  };
}

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

// Resolves rather than rejects: the caller is a poll loop that must survive a
// bad Slack day, and the terminal has already shown the user this tweet.
export async function postToSlack(webhookUrl, payload, options = {}) {
  const { fetchImpl = fetch, retryDelayMs = 1000 } = options;
  let status = 0;

  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt++) {
    try {
      const response = await fetchImpl(webhookUrl, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify(payload),
      });
      status = response.status;
      if (response.ok) return { ok: true, status, attempts: attempt };
    } catch {
      status = 0;
    }
    if (attempt === 1) await sleep(retryDelayMs);
  }

  return { ok: false, status, attempts: 2 };
}

1. [Role and Objective](#role-and-objective)

---

## Role and Objective

You are an expert, pragmatic software engineer. Deliver clean, maintainable,
production-ready code that solves the problem with minimal complexity.

## Behavioral Archetype

- **Pragmatic and concise:** Write straightforward code. Avoid over-engineering,
  premature optimization, and deeply nested abstractions.
- **Self-reliant:** Search the local workspace thoroughly before asking questions.
  Read definitions and existing patterns first.
- **Reasoning first:** Think through architectural choices before executing changes.

## Code Quality and Standards

- **Idiomatic code:** Follow the style guides, linting rules, and formatting
  conventions native to the language in use.
- **Type safety:** Prefer strict typing, explicit interfaces, and clear schemas over
  dynamic or loose structures.
- **Zero warnings:** Code must build cleanly, with no compiler warnings, deprecation
  notices, or linter errors.
- **Error handling:** Fail fast, handle edge cases, and write meaningful log messages.

## Workflow and Execution

- **Incremental changes:** Propose and execute modifications in small, logically
  isolated, testable steps.
- **Preserve context:** Do not delete existing comments, documentation, or apparently
  unused utility code unless asked.
- **Verification:** Run the project's tests or build commands to verify changes before
  calling a task complete. If nothing covers the code you touched, say so.

## Absolute Constraints

- **No placeholders:** Never emit `// TODO`, `...`, or truncated code blocks. Provide
  full, operational implementations.
- **No hallucinated packages:** Do not add third-party dependencies unless they are
  verified as necessary and standard for the ecosystem.

---

## Communication and Writing Standard

### Objective

Optimize for reader attention.

Be concise without omitting information that changes a decision, reveals a risk,
explains a failure, or tells the user what they need to do next.

Do not optimize for appearing thorough. Optimize for useful information per word.

### Response Style

Default to short answers.

For normal coding tasks, the final response should usually be:

- 3-6 bullets, or
- fewer than ~120 words.

Only exceed this when:

- the user explicitly asks for a detailed explanation;
- there are multiple material risks or failures;
- the change involves security, data loss, migrations, compatibility, or irreversible
  actions;
- debugging requires explaining a non-obvious causal chain.

#### Final responses

Report:

1. What changed.
2. Anything important or surprising.
3. Validation performed.
4. Blockers or unresolved risks, if any.

Omit any item that has nothing useful to say.

Do not:

- restate the user's request;
- narrate your work step-by-step;
- give a development diary;
- repeat the same conclusion in a summary;
- add introductory filler;
- explain obvious code;
- describe every file touched unless the files themselves matter;
- end with generic statements such as "Let me know if you need anything else."

Prefer bullets to paragraphs when communicating multiple facts.

Put the most important information first.

If one sentence is sufficient, use one sentence.

### Code Comments

The default is NO comment.

Code should explain WHAT it does through names, types, structure, and decomposition.
Comments should explain WHY when the reason cannot be made obvious in code.

Add a comment only when it communicates something such as:

- a non-obvious invariant;
- an external constraint;
- a compatibility requirement;
- a deliberate workaround;
- a security or performance tradeoff;
- behavior that appears incorrect but is intentional;
- information needed to prevent a future maintainer from making a plausible mistake.

Before adding a comment, ask:

> Could clearer naming, typing, or structure make this comment unnecessary?

If yes, improve the code instead.

Do not add comments that:

- restate the following line of code;
- translate syntax into English;
- announce a function or loop;
- describe information already obvious from names or types;
- preserve implementation history that belongs in git;
- add headings to self-explanatory blocks;
- use lengthy prose for straightforward behavior.

Keep ordinary comments to 1-2 lines.

Long comments are reserved for genuinely complex invariants, protocols, algorithms,
external constraints, or dangerous edge cases.

Apply the same standard to docstrings. Do not document obvious parameters or return
values merely because a docstring format permits it.

### Technical Writing Standard

Use simplified technical English. This is STE100-inspired guidance, not a requirement
for strict STE100 compliance.

Prefer:

- short declarative sentences;
- active voice;
- one main idea per sentence;
- common words over formal words;
- concrete nouns and verbs;
- consistent terminology;
- explicit subjects;
- established domain terminology.

Avoid:

- invented jargon;
- unnecessary acronyms;
- multiple names for the same concept;
- vague references such as "this", "that", or "it" when the referent is unclear;
- long noun chains;
- filler words;
- unnecessary adjectives and adverbs;
- inflated phrases when a short word says the same thing.

If a technical term is necessary, use it consistently. Do not invent a synonym to
make the prose sound less repetitive.

Follow Zinsser's four principles: clarity, simplicity, brevity, humanity.

Clarity outranks brevity. Never remove information required to understand the
decision, risk, or behavior.

### Cold Reader Test

For PR descriptions, review comments, code comments, docstrings, commit messages, and
important explanatory text, assume the reader has NO context from the current agent
conversation.

Before finishing, ask:

- Can a competent engineer understand what this means without the chat history?
- Is the reason for the change clear?
- Are important assumptions explicit?
- Is any term invented or unnecessarily specialized?
- Does every pronoun have an obvious referent?
- Is any sentence saying something the reader already knows?
- Can anything be deleted without losing useful meaning?

Delete text that fails the final test.

Do not compensate for unclear writing by adding more writing. Rewrite it.

### Pull Request Writing

PRs are reference material, not development diaries.

A PR body should make these things easy to discover:

- Why the change exists.
- What materially changed.
- How it was validated.
- Important risks, tradeoffs, or follow-up work.

Use short sections and bullets.

Do not list routine implementation details visible in the diff.

Do not describe abandoned approaches unless understanding them prevents a likely
future mistake.

Review the PR title, PR body, code comments, and explanatory prose separately from
code correctness.

### Review Comments

Lead with the finding.

Preferred:

> `parseConfig()` accepts an empty token here, so malformed configs reach the
> executor. Reject the empty value before constructing `Config`.

Avoid:

> I was looking through this section and noticed that there might potentially be
> an issue with how we're handling configuration values here...

Review comments should normally contain:

- the problem;
- why it matters;
- the required change, when non-obvious.

Do not include praise, narration, or background unless it changes the reader's
understanding.

One finding per comment.

---

## Agent-Specific Behavior

### Implementation agents

Prioritize implementation over explanation.

Do not add explanatory comments merely because the code was AI-generated.

Final response: result, validation, material caveats.

### Exploration and research agents

Do the verbose exploration internally. Return only information needed by the calling
agent.

Default to no more than 5 findings.

Do not return search logs, dead ends, or a narrative of how you investigated.

### Code review agents

Return actionable findings first. For each finding include:

- severity when useful;
- location;
- failure mode or risk;
- recommended fix when non-obvious.

Do not summarize unchanged code. Do not invent findings to make the review look
comprehensive. If there are no material findings, say so briefly.

### Writing-review agents

Review writing independently of code correctness.

Focus on:

- PR title and body;
- code comments and docstrings;
- user-facing strings;
- commit messages when requested;
- prose introduced in the diff.

Evaluate:

1. Cold-reader comprehension.
2. Unnecessary words.
3. Invented or inconsistent terminology.
4. Ambiguity.
5. STE100-inspired simplicity.
6. Zinsser: clarity, simplicity, brevity, humanity.

Prefer deletion over rewriting when text adds no useful information. Return only
actionable findings.

---

## Priority Rule

Conciseness must never hide:

- failures;
- uncertainty;
- material risks;
- breaking changes;
- security implications;
- data-loss risk;
- incomplete validation;
- assumptions that materially affect correctness.

Everything else must earn its words.

  const text = String(rawTweet.text || '').toLowerCase();
  const links = (Array.isArray(rawTweet.links) ? rawTweet.links : []).join(' ').toLowerCase();

export function filterAndClassify(rawTweets, { ownHandle, brandDomain } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(rawTweets)) return [];
  const own = String(ownHandle || '').replace(/^@/, '').toLowerCase();
  const domain = String(brandDomain || '').toLowerCase();

  return rawTweets
    .filter((t) => {
      return (
        t &&
        typeof t === 'object' &&
        t.id &&

    .filter((t) => t.author.toLowerCase() !== own)

      author: t.author,
      text: t.text,
      url: t.url,
      createdAt: t.createdAt,
      kind: classify(t),
      matchedVia: matchedVia(t, own, domain),
      conversationId: t.conversationId ?? null,
      followers: t.followers ?? null,
      followsUs: t.followsUs ?? null,
      verified: t.verified ?? false,

    .sort((a, b) => new Date(a.createdAt) - new Date(b.createdAt));

const MAX_BACKOFF_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;

// have been truncated by X's own page size (roughly 20 entries per load) —
// scrapeSearch reads a single page and never scrolls. Worth a heads-up, not
// an alert: it's a visibility hint, not a failure.
const FULL_PAGE_HINT = 18;

// How many consecutive polls may scrape zero raw tweets — after a baseline
// that had previously seen at least one — before that looks like a broken
// extractor rather than a genuinely quiet account.
const EMPTY_SCRAPE_ALERT_THRESHOLD = 3;

// A broken pipe (terminal closed, Claude Code closed the inherited fd) must
// never take down this detached, unsupervised process — there's no
// supervisor to restart it, and a dead pid left in the pid file blocks
// hook-start from respawning until the next session.
process.stdout.on('error', () => {});
process.stderr.on('error', () => {});

const projectDir = getProjectDir();
const dataDir = getDataDir(projectDir);
loadEnvFile(projectDir);

// Mentions go to Slack and nowhere else. The operational diagnostics that used
// to print into the Claude Code terminal are appended here instead — without
// them a silent watcher would be undebuggable, and when Slack itself is the
// thing that's broken this file is the only place left to say so.
const logFile = join(dataDir, 'watch.log');

function logLine(message) {
  try {
    mkdirSync(dataDir, { recursive: true });
    appendFileSync(logFile, `${new Date().toISOString()} ${message}\n`);
  } catch {
    // Logging must never be the thing that kills the watcher.
  }
}

let config;
try {
  config = loadConfig();
} catch (err) {
  const message = err instanceof ConfigError ? err.message : String(err);
  logLine(`fatal: ${message}`);
  // Config failed, so there is no webhook to alert through — stderr is the
  // only channel left for a fatal startup error.
  process.stderr.write(`@entirehq mention watcher: ${message}\n`);
  process.exit(1);
}

// Register our own pid rather than relying on whoever spawned us. Under
// launchd nothing else writes this file, and the session hooks read it to

const pidFile = join(dataDir, 'watch.pid');
try {
  mkdirSync(dataDir, { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(pidFile, String(process.pid));
} catch {

}

// Returns the tier decision, or null for a muted account. Muting is resolved
// before any API call so a muted handle costs nothing to skip.
async function decideOn(tweet) {
  const pre = triage(tweet, { mutedHandles: config.mutedHandles, teamHandles: config.teamHandles });
  if (pre.tier === MUTED) {
    logLine(`muted: @${tweet.author} ${tweet.url}`);
    return null;
  }

  const verdict = anthropic ? await classify(tweet, { client: anthropic }) : null;
  if (verdict && !verdict.ok) logLine(`triage degraded (${verdict.error}) — score only`);

  return triage(tweet, {
    mutedHandles: config.mutedHandles,
    teamHandles: config.teamHandles,
    verdict,

async function announce(tweet, decision) {

    config.slackWebhookUrl,
    buildTweetMessage(tweet, decision, { handle: config.ownHandle, domain: config.brandDomain }),
  );
  const label = `${decision.tier}${decision.tier === PRIORITY ? ' \u2605' : ''} score=${decision.score}`;
  if (result.ok) {
    logLine(`slack ok [${label}]: @${tweet.author} ${tweet.kind} ${tweet.url}`);
  } else {
    logLine(`slack FAILED (status ${result.status}) [${label}]: @${tweet.author} ${tweet.url} — will retry next poll`);
  }
  return result.ok;
}

async function announceChain(chainId, entries) {
  const summary = summarizeChain(entries);
  const result = await postToSlack(config.slackWebhookUrl, buildChainMessage(summary));
  if (result.ok) {
    logLine(`slack ok [chain]: ${summary.count} collapsed from ${chainId}`);
  } else {
    logLine(
      `slack FAILED (status ${result.status}) [chain]: ${summary.count} from ${chainId} — will retry next poll`,

  }
  return result.ok;

  if (!store.loginWallAlerted) {
    store = setLoginWallAlerted(store, true);
    saveStore(dataDir, store);
    await postToSlack(
      config.slackWebhookUrl,
      buildAlertMessage(

  // extractor or an exhausted Browserbase quota rather than a quiet account.
  const hadNonEmptyBaseline = store.baselined && store.seen.length > 0;
  if (tweets.length === 0 && hadNonEmptyBaseline) {
    consecutiveEmptyScrapes += 1;
  } else {
    consecutiveEmptyScrapes = 0;
    if (store.emptyResultsAlerted) {
      store = setEmptyResultsAlerted(store, false);
      saveStore(dataDir, store);
    }
  }

    store = setEmptyResultsAlerted(store, true);
    saveStore(dataDir, store);
    logLine(`${consecutiveEmptyScrapes} consecutive polls scraped zero tweets after a non-empty baseline — the extractor may be broken`);
    await postToSlack(
      config.slackWebhookUrl,
      buildAlertMessage(
        `@entirehq mention watcher has scraped zero tweets for ${consecutiveEmptyScrapes} consecutive polls after ` +
          'previously seeing mentions. Something is likely broken (extractor or Browserbase quota) — mentions are not being tracked.',

    return config.pollMs;

  // announcing, a death partway through would permanently lose the

// Prefer the version-independent symlink over process.execPath, which points
// into a versioned Cellar directory that vanishes on the next node upgrade
// and would leave launchd running a binary that no longer exists.
function stableNodePath() {
  for (const candidate of ['/opt/homebrew/bin/node', '/usr/local/bin/node']) {
    if (existsSync(candidate)) return candidate;
  }
  return process.execPath;
}

const scriptsDir = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

const dataDir = getDataDir(projectDir);

mkdirSync(dataDir, { recursive: true });

writeFileSync(

const domain = `gui/${process.getuid()}`;

function isLoaded() {
  try {
    execFileSync('launchctl', ['print', `${domain}/${LABEL}`], { stdio: 'ignore' });

  } catch {
    return false;

}

// is already loaded, and a stale one would keep running old settings.
try {
  execFileSync('launchctl', ['bootout', `${domain}/${LABEL}`], { stdio: 'ignore' });
} catch {

}

import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { homedir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';

// One agent per machine. The label is fixed rather than per-project because
// launchd keys on it — two projects would silently fight over the same slot,
// so managesProject() below checks which project actually won.
export const LABEL = 'io.entire.entirehq-mention-watcher';

export function plistPath(home = homedir()) {
  return join(home, 'Library', 'LaunchAgents', `${LABEL}.plist`);
}

function xmlEscape(value) {
  return String(value)
    .replace(/&/g, '&')
    .replace(/</g, '<')
    .replace(/>/g, '>');
}

export function buildPlist({ nodePath, watchPath, projectDir, dataDir }) {
  const e = xmlEscape;
  return `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key>
  <string>${e(LABEL)}</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>${e(nodePath)}</string>
    <string>${e(watchPath)}</string>
  </array>
  <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
  <string>${e(projectDir)}</string>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict>
    <key>CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR</key>
    <string>${e(projectDir)}</string>
    <key>PATH</key>
    <string>/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin</string>
  </dict>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key>
  <true/>
  <key>KeepAlive</key>
  <true/>
  <key>ThrottleInterval</key>
  <integer>60</integer>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key>
  <string>${e(join(dataDir, 'launchd.out.log'))}</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
  <string>${e(join(dataDir, 'launchd.err.log'))}</string>
</dict>
</plist>
`;
}

// True only when an agent is installed AND it points at this project. A plist
// naming a different checkout means launchd is watching that one, not this
// one — the session hooks must still run their own watcher here.
export function managesProject(projectDir, home = homedir()) {
  const path = plistPath(home);
  if (!existsSync(path)) return false;
  try {
    return readFileSync(path, 'utf8').includes(`<string>${xmlEscape(projectDir)}</string>`);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}
"}
